pool.name: find_sounds
pool.description: Find sounds on this computer by words in their file and folder names ("kick", "808", "vinyl"), or pick some at random. Searches the folders the producer names, as full paths or ~/…, and otherwise where Live keeps samples: the User Library, Live's Core Library and Factory Packs. Returns each sample's name, path and length in seconds (for WAV and AIFF).

pool.name: make_device
pool.description: Make a Max for Live device the producer asks for: a MIDI effect, an audio effect or an instrument. Kumi writes it to their User Library for load_device. Read the guide for the kind first (guide: true, type): what the device's code can use, the rules Kumi checks, and what makes a device good. Then give its type, name, what it does, its controls (knobs, menus and switches, which become ordinary Live parameters) and its code: JavaScript for a MIDI effect (with tests Kumi runs), GenExpr (Max's gen~) for an audio effect or one voice of an instrument. Kumi builds the device around the code, checks it, and refuses a device that breaks a rule, saying why so you can fix it. Build what the producer asks for, as fully as they ask: as many controls as it needs, and the original's behaviour when recreating one. Kumi's rules keep a device safe and loadable; they don't limit its scope, and its ceilings are generous. Then load it with load_device and the itemId it returns, and hear an audio effect or instrument with audition.

guide.description: true: read how to make a device of this type (first)

type.description: midi_effect (JavaScript), audio_effect or instrument (GenExpr); midi_effect when left out

name.description: The device's name, as the producer would say it

about.description: What it does, in a sentence or two

default.description: A number, one of the options, or true/false

code.description: A MIDI effect's JavaScript (function midi(event) and helpers), or an audio effect's or one instrument voice's GenExpr (see the guide)

voices.description: An instrument's voices: how many notes play at once, 1 for mono (8 when left out)

runs_free.description: A MIDI effect that keeps sending on its own once every note is released (an LFO, a clock, a generator)

pool.name: set_tempo
pool.description: Change the Set's tempo in BPM (20–999).

pool.name: set_mixer
pool.description: Change one track's mixer. volume is the fader position from 0 to 1 (0.85 is 0 dB, 1 is +6 dB); pan goes from -1 (left) to 1 (right); mute and solo are on/off; sends are levels from 0 to 1 for return tracks A, B, … in order (a shorter list leaves the rest). trackRef comes from discovery in this turn; return tracks and the main track work too.

pool.name: rename
pool.description: Rename a track, scene, clip, device or locator. kind says which; ref comes from discovery in this turn.

pool.name: add_tracks_and_scenes
pool.description: Add new MIDI or audio tracks and named scenes. New ones go after the last track or scene unless you give an index (0 is first). References from earlier in this answer still name the same tracks and scenes afterwards; the answer says when they don't.

pool.name: load_sample
pool.description: Load a sample into a new Simpler on an empty MIDI track (add the track first): one change, undone as one. sample is the path of an audio file (one find_sounds returned, or any on this computer); trackRef comes from discovery in this turn or the track just added.

sample.description: The path of an audio file (one find_sounds returned, or any on this computer), or {"random": true, "words": ["kick"]} for Kumi to pick one itself (words and folders optional)

pool.name: load_sample_to_pad

note.description: The pad: 36 is C1, the first pad

sample.description: The path of an audio file (one find_sounds returned, or any on this computer), or {"random": true, "words": ["kick"]} for Kumi to pick one itself (words and folders optional)

instrument.description: Simpler unless the producer asks for Drum Sampler

pool.name: load_device
pool.description: Load an instrument, effect, Max for Live device or preset from Live's Browser onto a track (after its devices) or, with chainRef instead, into a rack's chain (after the chain's devices; a chain can hold a rack too). itemId is the Browser path, such as "instruments/Drum Rack", "instruments/Operator", "audio_effects/Reverb" or a modulator, "modulators/LFO" (and Shaper, Envelope Follower, Expression Control); live_browser_search finds others. A track or a chain takes one instrument: to layer instruments, load an Instrument Rack, add a chain for each with edit_rack, and load one into each. trackRef and chainRef come from discovery in this turn or an earlier step.

pool.name: set_device_parameter
pool.description: Set one device parameter to a value between its min and max, or several of one device at once with values (one change, one undo) when offered. deviceRef and parameterRef come from discovery in this turn; instead of parameterRef, parameter names it ("Drive"), found on the device when the step runs: that's how a plan or a recipe sets a device an earlier step loaded (deviceRef "@sat").

parameter.description: The parameter's name on the device, as Live shows it; instead of parameterRef

pool.name: edit_rack
pool.description: Work on a rack (instrument, audio effect, MIDI effect or drum rack): add-chain (chains play side by side, in parallel; mark it with as and load devices into it with load_device's chainRef; index 0 is first), add-macro or remove-macro, randomize-macros (Live's Rand button), store-variation (the macros' current settings, as a new variation), recall-variation or delete-variation (index), select-variation (index), or copy-pad (a drum rack's pad sourceIndex to targetIndex, notes 0–127). rackRef is the rack from discovery in this turn or an earlier step. Macro values are the rack's "Macro 1", "Macro 2", … parameters: set them with set_device_parameter.

index.description: add-chain: where the chain goes, 0 is first (left out, after the last); variations: which one, 0 is first

pool.name: set_chain_mixer
pool.description: Balance a rack's chains: one chain's volume (0 to 1; 0.85 is 0 dB), pan (-1 left to 1 right), or chainActivator false to switch the chain off (true on). chainRef comes from discovery in this turn or an earlier step.

pool.name: set_locators
pool.description: Mark a section in the Arrangement with two named locators. start and end are in beats from the start of the song (bar 1 is beat 0; a 4/4 bar is 4 beats).

pool.name: set_track_color
pool.description: Change a track's colour to one of Live's 70 palette colours (colorIndex 0–69). ref comes from discovery in this turn.

pool.name: set_transport
pool.description: Change the transport: the loop (loopEnabled, loopStart and loopLength in beats; a 4/4 bar is 4 beats), the metronome, punch in and out, and the playhead position (beats). Playing and stopping are the play tool's.

pool.name: set_routing
pool.description: Route a track and get it ready to record: its input (inputType and inputSubRouting, such as another track and "Post FX", or "Resampling" for the main output; never "Main", which crashes Live) and output (outputType, outputSubRouting), exactly as Live names them (live_discover kind routing-choice with the track as parent lists them), arm on or off, and monitoring in, auto or off. A new audio track fed by another track and armed is how audio gets bounced (resampling).

pool.name: set_mixer_options
pool.description: A track's other mixer settings: trackActivator (the track on or off), crossfadeAssign (0 none, 1 A, 2 B), panningMode (0 stereo, 1 split) with panningLeft and panningRight (-1 to 1), and the main track's crossfader (-1 A to 1 B).

pool.name: edit_rack_mapping
pool.description: Experimental Willington rack edits: kind macro-name renames macroIndex 0–15; variation-name renames the selected variation; macro-mapping assigns targetRef to mappingIndex 0–15 with minimum, maximum and mappingKind continuous, enum or boolean. Null mappingIndex unmaps. Boolean endpoints are macro thresholds 0–127; others use target parameter units. Kinds key-zone, velocity-zone and selector-zone edit one regular chain: ref is its parent rack, targetRef the chain; minimum, maximum, fadeMinimum and fadeMaximum are integer endpoints. Omitted endpoints retain their current values; supply an ordered complete range, with velocity 1–127 and key/selector 0–127. Audio Effect Racks support selector zones only; Instrument and MIDI Effect Racks support all three. Requires stopped playback.

pool.name: set_clip_follow_actions
pool.description: Set Session clip Follow Actions with experimental Willington support. Requires stopped playback. Actions: 0 none, 1 stop, 2 again, 3 previous, 4 next, 5 first, 6 last, 7 any, 8 other, 9 jump. Chances are percentages; supplying one sets the complementary chance. Linked timing uses loop count; unlinked time uses beats. Jump targets are 1-based scene numbers. For launch Legato, use set_clip with legato: true after creating the clip. Does not change scene Follow Actions or the global switch.

pool.name: set_clip
pool.description: Change a clip's settings: muted, colorIndex (0–69), looping with loopStart and loopEnd (beats from the clip's start), launchMode (0 trigger, 1 gate, 2 toggle, 3 repeat), launchQuantization (0 global, then none, 8 bars, 4, 2, 1 bar, 1/2, 1/2T, 1/4, 1/4T, 1/8, 1/8T, 1/16, 1/16T, 1/32), legato, ramMode and velocityAmount (0–1). clipRef comes from discovery (a clip-slot's clipRef).

pool.name: edit_clip
pool.description: Edit a clip's content: crop (to its loop), duplicate-loop (doubles the loop, content and all), duplicate-region (copies regionStart–regionEnd to destination, in beats), or move-playing-position (by offset beats). Live gives Kumi no undo for these (Live's own undo can).

pool.name: duplicate_clip
pool.description: Copy a clip: into a Session slot (targetTrackRef and targetSceneIndex, 0 is the first scene; the same track when targetTrackRef is left out) or into the Arrangement at arrangementPosition (beats; a 4/4 bar is 4 beats). This is also how MIDI reaches the Arrangement: write the clip in Session view, then duplicate it there.

pool.name: set_automation
pool.description: Draw automation inside a Session clip for one device parameter: create-envelope, then insert points ({time in beats from the clip start, value in the parameter's own range}), insert-step (start and length in beats, value: one value held for that long; it makes the lane when there's none), delete-range (from, to), or delete-envelope. clipRef from discovery; parameterRef from discovering the device's parameters. The Arrangement's automation lanes aren't reachable.

pool.name: change_structure
pool.description: Add a return track (create-return, with a name), delete one (delete-return, ref; Live gives Kumi no undo for this), or duplicate a track or scene (duplicate-track, duplicate-scene, ref). References from earlier in this answer still name the same tracks and scenes afterwards, except sends once a return is deleted; the answer says when they don't.

pool.name: set_scene
pool.description: Change a scene: colorIndex (0–69), its own tempo (tempo with tempoEnabled) and time signature (signatureNumerator, signatureDenominator with timeSignatureEnabled), which Live switches to when the scene launches. ref is the scene from discovery.

pool.name: capture_scene

pool.name: switch_device

pool.name: move_device

pool.name: move_device_to

pool.name: set_chain

pool.name: set_song

pool.name: select

pool.description: Change what Live shows: focus-view with view Session, Arranger, Detail, Detail/Clip, Detail/DeviceChain or Browser; hide-view; zoom-in, zoom-out, scroll-left, scroll-right; follow-on, follow-off; collapse-track or expand-track (trackRef); browser-toggle.

pool.name: arrange
pool.description: Lay out an arrangement in the Arrangement from the producer's own clips, in one call: the sections in order, each with its name, its length in bars and the tracks that play in it, from Session scenes (a section plays a scene's clips, or chosen clips per track) or from a loop already in the Arrangement (loop: its bars; its MIDI clips are copied with their notes). Kumi copies the clips (whole loops, and a loop's first part where a section ends sooner), adds the gaps, fills and risers asked for, marks each section with a locator and puts the playhead at the start. It's one change: one line in HISTORY whose undo takes it all back, and one Cmd-Z in Live. Without sections it changes nothing and returns the material to plan with: each scene's clips by track with their lengths, where the Arrangement's clips end, and its locators. Vary it by subtraction and addition: tracks in and out per section; gap: tracks drop out for the last beats before the next section (the breath before a drop); fill: a track's other clip (its fill or a variation) in place of the loop's end; riser: a clip on an effects track (a riser, a sweep, a crash) placed to end where the section ends.

pool.name: undo_change
pool.description: Undo one of your changes from this session: pass its change id (such as c3), or "last" for the latest one. It only works while nobody changed the same thing in Live since; if so, say what happened. With final: true, when the undo is all that was asked, Kumi tells the producer and the answer ends there, with no reply from you.

change.description: A change id such as c3, or "last"

final.description: true when the undo completes the request: Kumi tells the producer, and the answer ends there

pool.name: watch_me
pool.description: Learn a routine the producer does by hand in Live: action start just before they do it (Kumi notes the Set as it is; nothing in Live changes), then action stop when they say they're done. Stop gives what changed: tracks added (with routing, arming, monitoring), devices loaded (with the knobs they turned from Live's defaults; switches and modes aren't compared), clips recorded or made, and settings changed, each with its track. Save it at once with save_recipe as the steps that would redo it, with $blanks for what differs each time (the source track, say), leaving out anything clearly unrelated: a device as load_device (as: "sat") and each knob turned as set_device_parameter with deviceRef "@sat" and the knob's name as parameter. Then say in a few words what the recipe does. The producer can ask you to change it.

pool.name: audition
pool.description: Hear what you built, quietly, and how close it is to a reference, in one call: Kumi plays the part with Main silenced and hears each candidate track after its devices, compares it with the reference, then puts everything back. Up to 8 candidates are heard together in one real-time pass, so try several ideas at once (different instruments, chains, settings on separate tracks). Say where the part is: from_beat and beats in the Arrangement, or a Session clip per candidate (clip), which Kumi plays from the Arrangement for the render and removes after. A candidate can be the whole mix ({"mix": true}, on its own): what Main plays at from_beat, heard as quietly as a track; audition it against a reference to match a mix, changing EQ, compression and levels between rounds. Returns each candidate's closeness to the reference (0–100) with the biggest gaps in words, and what it heard. A silent render is reported, not compared. Without a reference it only listens.

candidates.description: The tracks to render, each on its own (a candidate sound, or the track to check), or the whole mix

mix.description: true: the whole mix (Main's output) instead of a track

clip.description: A Session clip on that track to play (its clipRef); left out, the Arrangement at from_beat

label.description: A short name for it ("Collision + parallel delay")

from_beat.description: Where the part starts in the Arrangement, in beats (a 4/4 bar is 4)

beats.description: How long to render, in beats; a clip's length when left out, 8 at most by default

reference.description: What to match: an audio file's path or ~/…, or an audio clip's clipRef

reference_from_seconds.description: Where in the reference the part is

reference_seconds.description: How much of the reference to hear

focus.description: sound: one patch or hit (timbre, envelope, pitch); section: a part or mix (balance, density, rhythm too). Left out, by length

pool.name: render
pool.description: Render an audio track's own clips (its recordings, a bounce) between two points to a file at once: offline and silent, no transport, no recording. It's the raw audio, before the track's devices; instruments, effects and the mix aren't in it (for those, audition, or record by resampling). Returns the file for listen, to hear it or compare it with a reference.

track.description: An audio track (its reference from this turn)

from_beat.description: Where to start in the Arrangement, in beats (a 4/4 bar is 4)

pool.name: undo_in_live
pool.description: Live's own undo (or redo, with redo: true), once, exactly like Cmd-Z in Live: for something the producer did in Live themselves, or a change of Kumi's that undo_change can't take back (a crop, or a change undo_change says it can't). For Kumi's other changes use undo_change, which undoes exactly that change; this undoes whatever Live did last.

pool.name: run_python
pool.description: Run Python inside Live for anything your typed tools don't cover; use those first. Explore Live's API with dir(). mode eval returns an expression; exec (default) returns whatever you assign to result. Names: Live, song, app, obj (optional ref), bridge. Returns JSON {ok, result, stdout, error}, with Live objects as usable {ref, type, name} and errors as type, message and traceback. Each run opens one step in Live's undo or joins an already open step; undo_in_live takes it back. No HISTORY entry or undo_change. Set reads and old references are discarded after every run, including failures. timeoutMs defaults to 5000 (1–30000), checked by Python tracing; native calls finish before the deadline can be checked.

pool.name: live_command
pool.description: Use Live's own commands, through its menus and keys, for what your other tools can't do: group or ungroup tracks, freeze, unfreeze or flatten a track, bounce a track or clip to audio without playing it (bounce_to_new_track, bounce_track_in_place), consolidate, convert an audio clip to MIDI (melody, harmony, drums), separate stems, slice to a MIDI track, save the Set (or collect all and save), save it as a new file (save_as with path), start a new Set (new_set) or open one (open_set with path), export audio or a MIDI clip. new_set and open_set replace the open Set: say what happens to its unsaved changes with save_current (ask the producer when they didn't say), and references from before are gone once it's open: its answer then has the Set as it is (now), with current references, so carry on in it. Give final: true to the command that finishes the request (a save, a save as, the new Set) and Kumi tells the producer itself. Kumi fills Live's Save and Open dialogs on Windows only: on a Mac, ask the producer to save as or open a Set in Live. When a file is already at path, Live asks before replacing it: ask the producer, never answer it yourself. Live keeps a Set in a project folder: saved as into a folder that isn't one, it makes "<name> Project" there, and the result says where the Set went. Never make or edit .als files yourself: Live calls a Set it didn't write corrupt. Give the command and what it works on (track, tracks side by side, or clip): Kumi selects it in Live, presses the command, and says what changed. For anything else Live's menus or keys do, give menu (the item's titles, ["Create", "Insert Silence"]) or keys (["cmd+e"]). pool.name: judge
pool.description: Work toward a sound goal in rounds, as an engineer would: Kumi listens, finds the biggest gap, you make one change, and Kumi keeps it only if the evidence says so. Start a run with goal: what to reach (loudness in LUFS, a true_peak ceiling in dBTP), a reference (an audio file or clip whose tonal balance, dynamics and low end become targets, each with its range), focus (a track that must cut through: masking is measured against it) and explicit targets. Kumi hears the mix (or track) quietly once and answers with the checklist: each item's value, what it wants and how many just-noticeable steps it's off, the problems it found placed in time and frequency (harsh hits at 0:42, 5.8–7.2 kHz, +9 dB over the local level; a steady resonance; stereo lows; one bass note louder than the rest; the vocal buried 1–4 kHz), and the next target with the kind of fix it calls for. Make ONE change toward that target with Live's devices, then call judge again with change saying what you did. Kumi hears the same bars again, compares every item at equal loudness, keeps the change only if its target improved and nothing else got audibly worse (it takes the change back itself otherwise: don't undo it yourself), brings loudness back to target, and names the next target. Let the problem pick the tool: a steady imbalance is a static EQ (EQ Eight), one that comes and goes is a dynamic band (Multiband Dynamics) or a de-esser, peaks are a limiter, wide lows are mono below a frequency (Utility's Bass Mono), a buried element is a dip in the others keyed from it. Fix a problem where it starts when you can (the hi-hats' harshness on the hi-hat track, not the master). When a target resists two changes in a row, Kumi moves on to the next and comes back to it later. Keep going until every item is within tolerance or changes stop helping (in a /loop, Kumi decides that and asks you), then call judge with done: true, which hears the whole stretch again and reports before → after.

goal.description: Starts a run (and ends any other)

reference.description: A reference: one measured with the reference tool (its name), an audio file's path (~/…) or an audio clip's clipRef

problems.description: Clear what Kumi's detectors find (true when left out)

sound.description: A single sound (a patch, a hit) against a reference sound: its attack, decay, where it settles, brightness, noisiness, pitch drop (an 808's or a kick's), modulation rate, width, top (bandwidth), noise floor, warmth (2nd and 3rd harmonics), tail and crackle join the checklist, and its effects: a reverb's decay time and how its tail darkens, echoes' time and fall, how deep it swings, how far its brightness sweeps and its tail's share. Judge it on the track that plays it (track)

focus.description: The track that must cut through the rest (its ref or name)

measure.description: dynamics: peak to loudness (dB); density: peak to short-term loudness (dB); range: loudness range (LU); punch: crest (dB); low_width: side under mid below 120 Hz (dB); rumble: under 30 Hz against 30–120 Hz (dB); brightness: tilt (dB per octave, 0 is pink); decay_time: a reverb's RT60 (s); tail_darkening: how much its tails darken (octaves); echo_time: ms between echoes; echo_fall: dB each echo falls; swing: modulation depth (dB); sweep: how far its brightness moves (octaves); tail_share: its tail's share of its energy (%)

track.description: Judge one track (its ref or name) instead of the mix

from_beat.description: Where the stretch starts in the Arrangement, in beats (the whole song when left out)

beats.description: How long the stretch is, in beats

change.description: What you changed since the last judge call, in one line

done.description: End the run: hear the whole stretch again and report before → after

pool.name: tune
pool.description: Code picks the numbers for a change you chose, against the judged run's checklist, and Kumi judges the result as a round (kept or taken back, like judge with change). Put the device where the fix belongs first (make_changes), then tune it. how: "fit" calculates an EQ Eight's bands from what was measured, with no trial listens: the smallest cut that clears a steady resonance or harshness, or bands that close the balance gaps toward the reference while holding the regions already in tolerance (it uses the EQ's free bands, and turns Adaptive Q off and Scale to 100% so they land as calculated). "home" moves one knob where more means more until its target is met, each probe heard on the target's excerpt: a limiter's gain toward a loudness, its ceiling toward a true peak, a de-esser's or dynamic band's threshold until the harsh hits drop, an EQ band's gain until the vocal stops being masked. "search" tunes 2–5 knobs that interact (a compressor's attack, release and ratio; a reverb's size, decay and damping) on the run's own track (judge with track; a plain track, not a group): small generations of candidates, each generation heard side by side on scratch copies of the track in one pass, and kept only if one beats where the knobs are. The copies play without the focus track, so masking is homed in on, not searched. Prefer tune over guessing numbers yourself: it takes fewer listens.

device.description: The device's ref (from discovery or make_changes)

target.description: The checklist item it's for (its id, such as "loudness" or "resonance 1.1 khz"); the run's next target when left out

knobs.description: The knobs’ names as the device shows them: one for home (such as "Gain" or "Threshold"), 2–5 for search

change.description: What the change is, in a few words, for the log

pool.name: groove
pool.description: Shape a part's feel toward a reference's, judged on the notes with no listening: where each lane plays (kick, snare, hats, the rest; one lane for a pitched part), its timing step by step (push, swing, laid-back hats), its velocity accents, syncopation and fills. Start a run with clip (the part, a MIDI clip) and reference (a MIDI clip with the reference's notes). For a reference's drums: put the track in the Arrangement, separate its stems (live_command separate_stems), convert the drum stem to MIDI (live_command convert_drums_to_midi), and give that MIDI clip as reference and the drum stem's clip as audio: Kumi hears the stem and moves each converted hit onto its real onset. Then change the notes (change_notes, transform_midi swing, quantize) and call groove with change, or let code move the notes toward the reference's timing and accents with apply: true (amount 0–1, all the way when left out). Kumi keeps a change only if its target got closer and nothing else moved away, taking it back otherwise, and names the next target. done: true ends the run with before → after.

clip.description: Starts a run: the part, a MIDI clip's clipRef

reference.description: Starts a run: the reference's MIDI clip (its clipRef)

audio.description: The reference's drum stem (an Arrangement audio clip's clipRef): its hits' onsets refine the reference's timing

change.description: What you changed in the part, to judge it

apply.description: Code moves the part's notes toward the reference's timing and accents, then judges that

amount.description: With apply: how far (1, all the way, when left out)

done.description: Ends the run: before → after on every line

pool.name: form
pool.description: Lay out the song's form, heard. Kumi listens to the whole Arrangement quietly (or from_beat for beats) and reads it bar by bar: the energy curve (loudness, density, brightness, low end); the sections it falls into (their bars, role: intro, build, peak, break, verse or outro, and a letter shared by sections that sound alike); the turns between them (a drop or a fall, and what prepares it: a build, a gap or a riser); the intro and outro lengths and the bar the first hook starts on; which tracks play where, from the Arrangement's clips; and the problems a form can have: neighbouring sections without contrast, energy that plateaus, odd phrase lengths, a drop that arrives unprepared, a stretch left unchanged for 32 bars and more. With a reference (an audio file or a clip in the Set), its form too, read at this Set's bar length, and how the two differ. A whole-song listen takes as long as the song.

from_beat.description: Where to start, in beats (the Arrangement's start when left out)

beats.description: How long, in beats (to the song's last clip when left out)

reference.description: A song to compare the form with: an audio file or a clip in the Set (its clipRef)

pool.name: sound
pool.description: Measure sounds in Live: the tracks heard quietly side by side in one pass (8 bars from from_beat unless beats says). Each sound gets its attack, decay (and how it sits against a beat), sustain, brightness, noisiness, pitch drop (an 808's or a kick's), modulation rate (and the beats a cycle), warmth (2nd and 3rd harmonics, even against odd), width, top (bandwidth), noise floor, tail (a dry hit falls far, a reverberant one hangs on) and crackle, and its effects: a reverb's decay time (RT60) and how its tails darken and widen, echoes (their time as a note value, repeats, how far each falls and darkens), how deep it swings, how far its brightness moves (a filter sweeping) and how often, pumping against the beat, and its tail's share bar by bar. Plus its problems: clicks at note edges, DC, a note jumping out, tails cut off, echoes out of time, repeats that don't die away, tails burying the dry hits. Several tracks are judged as a kit too: a piece whose noise floor, top or grit sits apart, pieces piling up or a gap between them, decays ringing into the next hits, and pieces that sound the same. With against (a kick, say), how far each track ducks under it and how fast it comes back, and whether their hits interlock or collide. With key, how far each track's notes sit from it. To move a sound toward a reference sound, judge it with goal.sound.

tracks.description: The tracks to measure (names or refs)

against.description: A track the others duck under or play against (its name or ref)

key.description: The song's key, like "F# minor", "Bb major" or "D dorian"

from_beat.description: Where to listen from, in beats

beats.description: How long, in beats (8 bars when left out)
